details:
I think it'd be really useful for worlds to have access to persistence, not just being able to save users' data but also access other users' save data. 

But instead of giving worlds access to every user's individual persistence data file, we could have a separate persistence data file for the world itself. This would allow for users to save data to the world itself persistently and have it affect others. The Persistent Pool would be more limited in how much data it can save per player, since it's saving a lot more data overall. 

A great use case for this would be a high-scores list, each player automatically submits their highest score to the persistent pool and only updates it if the player gets a higher score (keeping most processing/saving, persistent or not, as local as possible). The pool then has a database of everyone's highest scores and can turn it into a functional scoreboard. 

Alternately, in a string-loading world like VRBricks, a persistent pool could be used to store users' strings for others to access (in VRBricks' case, community brick builds). 

As for the size, persistence can currently save up to 100kb per player. I think that since the point of a persistent pool is just saving basic values, 10kb would be more than enough, as that could hold about 10,000 characters. 

Strings would prove more difficult though. Looking at save strings from Bullet Time Agent and VRBricks, both use different encoding (BTA being fully Base64 plain-text at roughly 1KB per string whereas VRBricks uses lots of Unicode and can easily take up the full 10KB with a large enough build, the string I tested with was 5kb), so it's dependent on how much data is being packed, but depending on size can easily fit multiple strings (at the 1kb Base64 size, up to 7 without going over, whereas for VRBricks where strings can vary in size, a 10kb limit for all strings uploaded to the Persistent Pool without going over). Admittedly I don't have an example world-persistence use case for Bullet Time Agent, I was just using its string as an example.

Increasing the size from 10kb to 25kb would fit more data, but the less file size this system takes up, the better, given this is per-user for a game with thousands of users. (Quick calculations with an assumed playerbase of 30,000 10kb saves would only be about 300mb, with 25kb being about 750mb, but that's per-world.)

TL;DR- I'd like to suggest a separate persistence file for a world itself, that allows users to save a small amount of data (10-25kb per user) that could be accessed by other players. This would allow for worlds to create databases for high scores, community creations (using strings), and anything the creator might want players to be able to share with one another in-game.

Thank you for your consideration!
title: "Persistent Pool" for worlds (a separate persistent file that multiple users can save to)
